Coalesce fragmented flowpaths with their downstream same-mainstem neighbor

Source: R/repairs.R
coalesce_fragmented_flowpaths.Rd

After aggregation + PRD + restore, some flowpaths end up with severely fragmented divides (sliver-dominated MULTIPOLYGONs with tiny total area) while their line geometry is valid. The missing territory was absorbed by the same-mainstem downstream neighbor, so the line overshoots its divide. This pass merges such flowpaths into their immediate downstream neighbor when the merge is safe.

Merge rule: fp_up is absorbed into fp_down when ALL hold:

  1. fp_up.flowpath_toid == fp_down.flowpath_id (directly adjacent)

  2. fp_up.mainstem == fp_down.mainstem (same stream)

  3. No POI attached to fp_up (preserves POI=outlet semantics)

  4. fp_up's current line coverage by its own divide is below coverage_threshold

Chains cascade: if fp_up -> fp_mid -> fp_down and both fp_up and fp_mid are absorbable, all three merge into fp_down.

Usage

coalesce_fragmented_flowpaths(
  input_gpkg,
  flowpath_layer = "flowpaths",
  divides_layer = "divides",
  flowlines_layer = "flowlines",
  pois_layer = "pois",
  network_layer = "network",
  coverage_threshold = 0.9
)

Arguments

input_gpkg

Path to the intermediate GeoPackage.

flowpath_layer, divides_layer, flowlines_layer, pois_layer, network_layer

Layer names. Defaults match the pre-ngen pipeline.

coverage_threshold

fp_up coverage below this triggers merge candidacy (default 0.9).

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of {up, down} merge pairs.
